review_scope: All nine four-arm comparison sheets inspected. Medium inspected learned images 0-4 at 1600px and original/precorrection 3. Root inspected learned 5 at 1600px. Sheets 6-8 alone do not establish full-detail safety. These are subjective agent development observations, not human preference or independent evaluation.
data_role: Already-consumed 1600px RAW-neutral JPEG development images; reference 18 selected after the prior daisy result. No native RAW or independent generalization claim.
reference_claim: Author-reported Portra 400 photograph; output is uncalibrated reference appearance transfer.

rows.subject: snow courtyard
rows.judgment: No overall preference over original; learned adds warm whites and cyan-green shadows over precorrection, but broad cyan contamination and prominent blue flag remain concerning.

rows.subject: fruit and blocks
rows.judgment: Clear photographic colour failure. Banana, apple and orange distinctions substantially collapse already in precorrection; learned does not restore them and strengthens green shadows. Prefer original/simple.

rows.subject: daisies
rows.judgment: Conditionally attractive dark floral treatment. Learned improves organization over precorrection; soil and background are strongly cyan-green and other flowers lose colour distinctions. Selected example cannot establish general success.

rows.subject: garden and vineyard
rows.judgment: Prefer original; precorrection is more readable than learned. Learned darkens foreground further and exaggerates blue flowers and orange distant field. Texture remains visible; do not equate dark appearance with confirmed pure-black clipping.

rows.subject: lakeside wood
rows.judgment: Learned has an identifiable low-chroma look, but prefer original water/sky colours. Warm wood and cyan water simplify reference relationships, with heavy green shadows.

rows.subject: sunflowers and bottles
rows.judgment: Prefer original. Yellow petals become pale cream and much of the bouquet loses its original colour separation during precorrection. Learned intensifies dark green/cyan while retaining visible petal, bottle and text structure; photographic colour failure, not established geometry failure.

rows.subject: red-brick station
rows.judgment: Prefer original. Blue sky and red brick become mostly cream/grey-green; learned adds contrast but does not restore distinct material colours. Comparison-sheet diagnosis only.

rows.subject: stonework and sculpture
rows.judgment: Prefer original warm materials. Precorrection removes warmth; learned deepens green shadows and cyan highlights. Comparison-sheet diagnosis only.

rows.subject: interior lamp and television
rows.judgment: No clear photographic benefit over original or precorrection. Warm lighting becomes cooler and green shadows heavier. Original highlights were already bright; no new clipping claim from the sheet alone.

decision: Not a convincing general photographic candidate on this consumed panel. No promotion or independent evaluation admission from this round. Preserve all outputs and investigate the causal contribution of global covariance/min-max precorrection before altering references.
next_question: Does the same fixed-reference pretrained model with the published NCC input path avoid the warm-object colour collapse? Requires separately declared bounded development ablation and correct model conditioning; applying an existing corrected-input LUT directly to original RGB is not the same experiment.
